body:
#1999 APPROVED at 3e5fd12ebf0d. YOU ASKED FOR A REVIEW CALL ON THE TRADE -
HERE IT IS, AND THE FRAMING IS THE ANSWER.

THE 5s -> 26s COMPARISON IS NOT A REGRESSION AND SHOULD NOT BE RECORDED AS
ONE. The 5s measured a function probing ~12 of 193 eligible candidates. It is
the cost of NOT DOING 94% OF THE WORK, not a baseline. There is no
correct-and-fast predecessor to regress from - 26s is the FIRST MEASUREMENT OF
THE CORRECT COMPUTATION.

AND THE SCALING IS REASSURING RATHER THAN ALARMING, which I think is the most
useful thing in this review: a ~16x widening of the candidate set costs ~5x
wall clock. That is SUB-LINEAR. A linear result would have been ~80s. So fixed
overhead dominates and the performance win is in the probe's SETUP, not in
trimming candidates. Whoever takes the performance work should start there.

SO, ON YOUR QUESTION - does a correctness fix that moves 5s to 26s satisfy a
spec whose subject is "the machine-readable path is unpollable"?

NO, AND IT MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS CLOSING BUG-1288. 26s is not pollable;
neither was 5s. This moves the command from FAST AND WRONG to SLOW AND RIGHT
and leaves the spec's headline criterion untouched. Correctness first is the
right call and I would not ask for a revert - the 134 Approved-status specs
whose branches were entirely unscanned are precisely the invisible work the
finding was about.

But the remaining work is now HARDER than when the spec was written: the
correct computation must be made fast over a candidate set 16x larger. That
belongs on the spec rather than being discovered by whoever picks it up
expecting a 5s starting point. AND IF THE TRAILER AT MERGE NAMES BUG-1288 IT
WILL AUTO-COMPLETE A SPEC WHOSE HEADLINE CRITERION IS UNMET - the five-state
predicate again, and this is the case it bites.

TWO THINGS I VERIFIED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED:

  THE PRINCIPLED-WIDENING CLAIM IS LITERALLY TRUE. Gate filters on
  "completed" | "rejected" | "superseded"; the downstream terminal check on
  the resolved spec_id filters on "completed" | "rejected" | "superseded".
  Byte-identical. Nothing is dropped at the gate for a reason that would not
  also drop it downstream.

  THE PER-TURN HOOK IS NOT AFFECTED - and I went looking for this, because a
  5x slowdown on every prompt in every session on this machine would be a real
  regression that no PR-level timing would surface. lib.rs:68554 gates the
  notice path behind notice_fast and SKIPS collect_unshipped_work_items
  entirely, with the latency contract stated in-code. The cost lands on
  --json and status --full only.

CREDIT WHERE IT IS UNUSUAL: they verified the binary sha before each timing
run, unprompted. That is the exact discipline whose absence produced my
BUG-1558 misfiling this morning, applied by a seat that was told about it once
in a brief. And the force-push was properly done - lease pinned to a freshly
FETCHED head, confirmed equal to my verdict's reviewed_sha, and they declined
to force over the gitlab mirror's rejection rather than flattening it.

PROBE RUN: Windows job still in_progress on 35637049540. I will send the
line-ending result the moment it is readable, including if it says LF.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #1999 approved - the 5s baseline was the cost of skipping 94% of the work, so this is not a regression. But BUG-1288 is NOT satisfied: do not let the trailer close it
